clue.text: Employees receiving nod resolved deadlock

indicators.note: the word for employees takes in the other letters, holding them inside

parts.note: staff are the employees of an organisation

indicators.note: resolved here means sorted out afresh, so the letters of nod are rearranged

explanation.surface: Workers greet a nod as the end of a standoff in negotiations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resolved' reads as settling the deadlock, but it is the signal to rearrange nod; the employees then hold those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A stand-off is a situation in which neither side can gain the advantage, an impasse.

clue.text: Propagandist distorted drop in cost

indicators.note: something distorted is twisted out of its shape, so the following letters are reshuffled

parts.note: all ten letters of these three words

explanation.surface: A propagandist misrepresents a price cut.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is apt: twisting the story of a price drop is exactly what a spin doctor does.
explanation.definitionFit: A spin doctor is a press agent who puts a favourable slant on news, a modern kind of propagandist.

clue.text: Fuss caused by commercial, then nothing

parts.note: an ad is a commercial
nothing is zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: An uproar provoked by an advert that then delivers nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Ado means bustle or trouble, as in much ado about nothing, a synonym for fuss.

clue.text: Beginning to doubt psychic power, express loss of hope

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter, so only that is kept

parts.note: the opening letter of doubt
extrasensory perception, abbreviated ESP
to air a view is to express it

explanation.surface: Starting to question one's psychic gifts and voicing hopelessness.
explanation.definitionFit: Despair is the complete absence of hope, so the noun phrase loss of hope matches it.

clue.text: Figure after fashion defending country honestly

indicators.note: after places the figure word at the end, following the rest
a defender surrounds and shields what it protects, so one word wraps the other

parts.note: a fad is a passing fashion
a country in the Middle East
a square is a geometric figure

explanation.surface: A political figure following a trend in defence of the nation, and doing so honestly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Figure' suggests a person or a number; here it is a geometric shape, placed last.
explanation.definitionFit: Fair and square is an idiom meaning openly and without cheating, used adverbially just like honestly.

clue.text: Bullet ends in target under tree

indicators.note: the ends of words are their final letters, so only the last of each is kept

parts.note: the closing letter of each of these two words
the acer is the maple genus

explanation.surface: A bullet finishing up in a target set below a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'under' looks like a positional instruction but is only a source of a final letter; the tree simply follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A tracer is a bullet with a burning charge that shows its trajectory, so it is one kind of bullet.

clue.text: Beef, say, about broadcast made ahead of time

indicators.note: the rearranged letters come before the letter for time

parts.note: re means about or concerning, as in a letter's 're:' line

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, so the letters of made are strewn into a new order

explanation.surface: A complaint, a beef, about a programme that was recorded in advance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beef' looks like a grumble, but here it is the food, and 'say' marks it as one example. RE, then MADE 'broadcast' as DMEA, comes 'ahead of' T.
explanation.definitionFit: Beef is one kind of red meat, along with lamb and venison, so beef is an example.

clue.text: Part from emperor endlessly breaking agreement

indicators.note: the shortened emperor breaks into the word for agreement, splitting it

parts.note: consent is agreement or permission

indicators.note: the name loses its final letter

parts.note: Titus was a Roman emperor

explanation.surface: A section taken from a ruler's decree that breached a treaty.
explanation.walkthrough: The emperor is Titus, the Roman emperor who completed the Colosseum; the surface invites a hunt for a longer imperial name.
explanation.definitionFit: A constituent is a component, one of the elements that make up a whole.

clue.text: Feel dizzy and look unpleasantly upset

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means turned upside down, so the word reads from bottom to top

parts.note: to leer is to look at someone in a nasty, suggestive way

explanation.surface: Someone feeling faint and looking ill and distressed.
explanation.definitionFit: To reel is to stagger or have the sensation of spinning, as when giddy or dizzy.

clue.text: Clubs in chains

definitions.meaning: first meaning: golf clubs with metal heads
second meaning: fetters or shackles for a prisoner

explanation.surface: Members of nightclubs, or card clubs, held in shackles.
explanation.definitionFit: Irons are both a class of golf club and metal shackles put on prisoners' legs or wrists.

clue.text: Company managed decline, losing large frequency

parts.note: Inc is the abbreviation for an incorporated company

indicators.note: managed here means handled and reworked, so the letters are rearranged
the letter for large is lost from the word decline before the rest is rearranged

parts.note: L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: A firm oversaw a downturn, shedding a big chunk of business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'managed decline' reads as a business phrase, but 'managed' is the anagram signal, worked on decline once 'losing' has removed the L.
explanation.definitionFit: Incidence is the rate at which something occurs, how often it happens.

clue.text: Solution mostly found in bond with man offering drink

indicators.note: with means alongside, so the man's word is added after the rest
the shortened word is placed within the word for bond

parts.note: cement is a binding substance, and to cement is to bond

indicators.note: most of the word, with its last letter dropped

parts.note: a remedy is a solution to a problem
he is the pronoun for a man

explanation.surface: A man finds the answer to a problem in a connection, and offers a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: The shortened remedy sits inside cement just after its first letter, and the man's pronoun follows; the accented spelling is French for 'cream of mint'.
explanation.definitionFit: Crème de menthe is a sweet green mint liqueur, a drink usually served after dinner.

clue.text: One dispute, a perfect example, beset by hollow scorn

indicators.note: beset means surrounded on all sides, so the hollow word wraps around everything before it

parts.note: a dent is a hollow in a surface
one is the Roman numeral I
to spar is to argue
taken as written
a gem is a perfect example of its kind

explanation.surface: A single argument, a model case, surrounded by empty contempt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hollow' looks like an adjective describing scorn, but it is the noun DENT and scorn is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Disparagement is belittling talk or contempt, so it is a synonym for scorn as a noun.

clue.text: Conceal pressure on places in film scripts

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means placed above, so the pieces follow one after another

parts.note: to screen is to hide from view
P is the symbol for pressure
to lay is to place something down

explanation.surface: Hiding pressure on locations used in films.
explanation.definitionFit: A screenplay is the written script of a film, so the plural matches film scripts.

clue.text: Architect crazy about singular style at home

indicators.note: about means around, so the crazy word goes round the others

parts.note: mad means crazy
S is the grammatical abbreviation for singular
to style something is to term or name it
someone at home is in

explanation.surface: An architect wild about a unique domestic style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Architect' looks like a building designer but is the person who plans a scheme; style is a verb, to name.
explanation.definitionFit: The architect of a plan is the person who devised it, which is what a mastermind is.

clue.text: Case about skill with clear, good English

parts.note: c, short for circa, means about
art is skill
to rid is to clear of something
G is the abbreviation for good
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: A legal case concerning skill, judged with clear, proper English.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Case' reads like a lawsuit but means a casing, the shell of a round of ammunition.
explanation.definitionFit: A cartridge is a casing holding the charge for a gun, or an ink container, so it is a case.

clue.text: Fish paste trader carries

indicators.note: something that carries holds a load inside, so the letters sit within the next words

parts.note: found running across the two words

explanation.surface: A merchant of fish paste going about his trade.
explanation.definitionFit: A tetra is a small brightly coloured tropical freshwater fish popular in aquariums.

clue.text: Plain across middle of plateau

parts.note: over means across, as in a bridge over a river

indicators.note: the middle of a word is its central letter, so only that one is kept

parts.note: the fourth of its seven letters

explanation.surface: A plain stretching right across the centre of a plateau.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plain' reads as flat land, matching plateau, but it is the adjective meaning obvious.
explanation.definitionFit: Overt means done openly and visible to all, so it is a synonym for plain in the sense of evident.

clue.text: Swindler's wits exercised on odd parts of theory

indicators.note: the rearranged letters sit on, in front of, the picked letters
exercised means worked over and put through its paces, so the letters of wits are rearranged
the odd-numbered letters of theory, the first, third and fifth

explanation.surface: A con man uses his cunning on bits of theory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exercised' turns WITS into TWIS, and 'odd parts of' theory give TER. A twister is British slang for a dishonest person.
explanation.definitionFit: A twister is a cheat or swindler, someone who twists the truth to deceive.

clue.text: Search clothing when that is most uncomfortable

indicators.note: clothing something means wrapping it round, so one word goes around the others

parts.note: a quest is a search
as means when, as in as I arrived
ie, from Latin id est, means that is

explanation.surface: Body searches with clothes on are the most awkward kind.
explanation.definitionFit: Queasy means nauseous or uneasy, so the superlative queasiest means feeling the most unwell or uncomfortable.

clue.text: Slight cut in region of atmosphere

indicators.note: in places the cut word inside the region word

parts.note: the sky is the region of air above us
to etch is to cut a design into a surface

explanation.surface: A small incision made somewhere in the air.
explanation.definitionFit: Sketchy means thin, lacking detail or substance, a synonym for slight as in slight evidence.

clue.text: Tax in store, price that's bad for part of nation's economy

indicators.note: the tax goes inside the rearranged letters
a bad version of the words is a corrupted one, so their letters are rearranged

parts.note: VAT is value added tax, the British sales tax

explanation.surface: A grumble that tax on shop prices is bad for the economy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'store, price' looks like the shopping scene, but the two words are the anagram fodder, with the British sales tax set among the rearranged letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The private sector is the businesses not owned or run by the state, one half of a mixed economy.

clue.text: Drop building in garden?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to cast off, as a tree does its leaves
second meaning: a small hut for tools at the end of a garden

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that a garden building is one example of the hut.
explanation.definitionFit: Shed is a verb meaning to let fall or lose, and a noun for a simple outbuilding used for storage.

clue.text: Profound corruption of real theft

indicators.note: corruption spoils the original form, so the following letters are rearranged

parts.note: all nine letters of these two words

explanation.surface: Deep-seated corruption amounting to actual stealing.
explanation.definitionFit: Heartfelt feelings are deeply and sincerely felt, so profound in the sense of intense applies.

clue.text: Crumbs soldier provided for dog

parts.note: crumbs and cor are both British exclamations of surprise
a GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: Good grief, a soldier has brought food for the dog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crumbs' looks like food for the dog but is a mild British exclamation, like cor.
explanation.definitionFit: The corgi is a short-legged Welsh breed of dog, famously kept by Queen Elizabeth II.

clue.text: Beam up in shiny armour

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters read from bottom to top
in says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: spanning the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: Sunlight glints off a knight's polished armour.
explanation.definitionFit: A ray is a narrow beam of light or radiation, so the two are synonyms.

clue.text: Walk out on wasteland

definitions.meaning: second meaning: a barren, arid region

explanation.surface: Abandoning someone in a barren landscape.
explanation.definitionFit: To desert is to abandon a person or duty, and a desert is dry barren land, two senses of one spelling.

clue.text: Innocent yen to follow river put into action

indicators.note: put into means placed inside, so the river and yen go within the action word

parts.note: a deed is an action

indicators.note: to follow means come after, so the yen letter is placed after the river

parts.note: the Wye is a river on the England-Wales border
Y is the symbol for the Japanese yen

explanation.surface: A naive person's longing set in motion.
explanation.definitionFit: Dewy-eyed means naively trusting or sentimental, like a child, so it fits innocent as an adjective.
